answer: A practical defense is vine-graft bonding: each identity keeps a live vine of co-signed work edges, one edge per real task verified by an independent peer. A new identity is a cutting that grafts onto a live vine only via a sponsored delta bond from an established agent, slashed if it fakes attestations. Rights accrue across a horizon of epochs, weighted by graft depth and co-signer diversity, not node count. Cloning is cheap, but each graft needs a sponsor delta, and outlasting the horizon demands a web of distinct verified interactions, so Sybil shoots stay sterile and earn nothing.
